question: pH at the Stage-2 coin electrodes' faces under their own current, in the media the letter allows
scope: coin half of the 00_07 HW.5.IS leg, plus the anchor ANODE conditional on a sap-filled gap; the anchor cathode waits on HW.53, and which gap state a living stem keeps is not known

sources.D_H: Apelblat & Barthel 1991, Z. Naturforsch. 46a, 131 (doi:10.1515/zna-1991-1-222): λ°(H⁺) = 349.85 at 25 °C as used on p. 135; 20 °C from Table 4 as Λ°(H₃Cit) − λ°(⅓Cit³⁻) = 390 − 64.04 (DERIVED — the 25 °C row holds the same identity, 422 = 349.85 + 72.05)
sources.D_O2: Han & Bartels 1996, J. Phys. Chem. 100, 5597 (doi:10.1021/jp952903y): log₁₀ D = −4.410 + 773.8/T − (506.4/T)², as printed in the ABSTRACT — the full text was not reached, and no second primary was read (Ferrell & Himmelblau 1967 · Wise & Houghton 1966 paywalled); Liu et al. use 1.99e-9 m²/s
sources.C_O2: USGS 2020, Techniques and Methods 9-A6.2 (doi:10.3133/tm9A6.2), Table 6.2-2, 760 mmHg, salinity 0 — built on Benson & Krause 1980/1984
sources.D_mal: NOT FOUND for malic acid or its anions — bracketed between a LARGER and a SMALLER dicarboxylate: the low end is hydrogen citrate as Liu et al. model it (SI Table S1), the high end hydrogen succinate (malate = hydroxysuccinate) from Apelblat & Barthel 1992, Z. Naturforsch. 47a, 493 (doi:10.1515/zna-1992-0309), λ°(HSucc⁻) = 47.0 on p. 497, flagged there as a best-fit value and above what a C4 monoanion should carry — likely high; both ends move to 20 °C with succinate²⁻'s own ratio, λ°(½Succ²⁻) 49.92 / 56.20 of Table 2
sources.delta_natural_convection: Katona et al. 2021, J. Electrochem. Soc. 168, 031512 (doi:10.1149/1945-7111/abeb29, open access), Introduction: δ under natural convection «from near 250 μm … to between 500 and 1000 μm» over the solutions it reviews; Amatore's aqueous ferrocyanide measurements 150–250 μm (the 135 μm it also lists is a DMF solution — left out); O₂ reduction in 0.6 M NaCl ≈ 800 μm

liu_fem_point.source: Liu et al. 2026, SI Fig. S4 (10 mM citrate, air, 300 s, centre of a 300 µm disk), read off the axes
liu_fem_point.bound: the linear regime only: in their 1 mM buffer the FEM redistributes current over the disk, which a uniform-flux film cannot; a planar 2 cm² face is far closer to the film

sap_pH4.5.what: the ratified sap brought to 4.5 — a laboratory's likeliest reading of the letter

sap_pH5.75.what: the ratified sap at its set-point — the cathode in a one-compartment cell

buffered_pH4.5.what: the sap's salts with malic acid at 10 mM, pH 4.5 — the letter's cathode medium since ⚖️ 2026-10-12

anode.glucose_transport: not computed — no free-solution D of glucose is sourced in the tree

states.sap_gap: the gap filled with sap, stagnant — computed below
states.air_gap: no electrolyte in the gap — 84 leaves it not modelled (layer 1 then runs through contact points only)
states.ingrown: wood in the gap: proton and malate transport through living sapwood has no source in the tree — not computed

sap_by_sku.pine: the pine point of 01_02 §2.1 (67 Q7) at pH 5.75 — pine, its topology variants, tropical and mangrove (whose own sap is not modelled)
sap_by_sku.beech_q8: 67 Q8 at pH 5.95 — broadleaf, and oak as a Fagaceae proxy (⚖️ founder 2026-10-18); its malate is solved from the potassium less the beech nitrate (KNO3 0.050 mM, Glavac & Jochheim 1993, ⚖️ 2026-10-22) — a ceiling on that side, while the buffers the recipe lacks push the other way

summer_acid_dates.why: the paper: they «coincided with the highest nitrate xylem sap concentration» (unpublished data then); printed in 1993, the nitrate on these dates is 1.20 · 1.01 · 0.94 mM, the 3 highest of the 26 dates against the point's 0.050 — carried beside the point as a reading, as the pH is; the 1990 paper does not report what acidifies the sap there, and the point's malate solve does not describe these dates

own_sap_reading.source: Van Die J., Willemse P.C.M. 1975, Acta Bot. Neerl. 24(2):237-239, doi:10.1111/j.1438-8677.1975.tb01013.x, Table 1 — Quercus rubra trunk xylem vessel sap, two trees, 27 Oct 1974, free outflow from the lowest stem cut, read from the page image

not_modelled: which medium and convection the laboratory will use (the letter fixes neither)
the pH inside the coatings — every shift here is a lower bound at the enzyme
a standard laccase buffer as the cathode medium
salting-out of O2 in the 0.25 M NaCl steps of test D (raises f)
the anode at 20 °C — L4's current is a 25 °C ceiling

the anchor anode's gap state in a living stem, the pH inside its gyroid lattice and the wood wall's own resistance (both lower its currents); migration, flow through the gap and a CO2/HCO3- buffer (each raises them); the anchor's working current after cold start — the EBFC's own P–V curve (HW.13)
